SUBSTITUTE NARRATIVE AND PLANS
TYPE I Rezoning Attachment #22852-T1
1855 West Grand Avenue
From M1-2 to B2-3

The Property
The subject property is a mixed-use building with ground floor commercial space and upper floor residential. The

surrounding area is comprised of varying zoning districts, including B1-3, B2-3, B3-3, RS-3, RT-4, RM-S, RM-
5, M1-2, and a large Planned Development. The area is improved with buildings of various ranging from 1 to 5
stories that contain multi-family residential, commercial, and industrial uses. The property is also a Transit Served
Location per the Transit Oriented Provisions of Chicago Zoning Ordinance (Section 17-10-0102-B (1)) as it is
within 2,310 feet of the CTA Danen Avenue Green Line train station entrance.

The Project
The Applicant proposes to demolish existing improvements and construct a four-story residential building with 4

dwelling units, 2-car attached garage, and 4 bicycle parking spaces. No commercial space is proposed. The zoning
height of the building will be 50.83 feet. To allow the proposed development, the Applicant seeks a zoning change
for the subject property from an M1-2 Limited Manufacturing/Business Park District to a B2-3 Neighborhood
Mixed-Use District. The Applicant is filing a Type 1 rezoning application and seeks all relief necessary, as allowed
by the Chicago Zoning Code, for the attached plans, including: 1) a variation under section 17-13-1101-B to
reduce the rear yard setback from the required 30 feet to 0 feet; 2) a variation under sections 17-13-1101-A and
17-13-1003-R to allow for a side building entrance; and 3) a variation under sections 17-13-1101-A and 17-13-
1003-L to increase the maximum building height by 1.7% from 50 feet to 50.83 feet.

17-3-0308 Specific Criteria for Transit Served Locations Requirements
1. The project complies with the applicable standards of Section 17-10-0102-B:

RESPONSE: The project complies with Section 17-10-0102-B as the property is a Transit Served
Location per the Transit Oriented Provisions of Chicago Zoning Ordinance (Section 17-10-0102-B (1))
as it is within 2,310 feet of the CTA Damen Avenue Green Line train entrance. The proposed
development does not include more than 50% of the otherwise required parking.

2. The project complies with the standards and regulations of Section 17-3-0504, except paragraph H if the
project is not located along a pedestrian street and except paragraph C if the land use is designated in a non-
commercial use group, pertaining to pedestrian streets and pedestrian retail streets, even if the project is not
located along a pedestrian street or a pedestrian retail street:

RESPONSE: The project is not along a pedestrian street, and except for requested variations, complies

with Section 17-3-0504 because:

° Building Location: The design complies with sections (1) and (2)(a)-(c), as the building’s setbacks
are no more than 5 feet, and the entrance size is within the required parameters;

© Doors and Entrances: While a variation is requested to allow for a side building entrance, the building’s
front doors will be set back no more than 3 feet;

© Off-Street Parking: 2. on-site automobile parking spaces will be provided;

e Parking Location: On-site parking will be enclosed in the rear of the lot; and

© Driveways and Vehicle Access: The Applicant will provide access to the parking garage to the rear
from a non-pedestrian street.

3. The project complies with the general goals set forth in the Transit Friendly Development Guide: Station Area
Typology, and any other station-specific plans, designs or guidelines adopted by the Chicago Plan
Commission:

RESPONSE: The property is near a station which has not been identified under the Transit Friendly
Guide station topography. However, the stop nearest east, the Ashland Green Line Station, is defined as
a Manufacturing Employment District, which provides that there is residential development potential—
which is the aim of the proposed project.

4. Residential building projects shall not have a number of parking spaces in excess of 50% of the Minimum
Automobile Parking Ratio for the applicable district listed in Section 17-10-0207 with any fractional result
rounded up to the next higher whole number, unless additional parking spaces are approved as
an administrative adjustment under the provisions of Section 17-13-1003-EE; and

RESPONSE: The project does not have parking in excess of 50% as only 2 spaces are proposed.

5. The project complies with the Travel Demand Study and Management Plan rules of the Chicago Department

of Transportation.
RESPONSE: The project will comply with applicable Travel Demand Study and Management Plan

rules promulgated by the Chicago Department of Transportation.
